primitives.name: Frozen Expert Ensemble
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Horde (team mmasana):** ensemble of feature extractors, each an expert trained on *one selected experience* (experiences with ≥5 classes; stop adding after 85% of classes seen; always train on experience 1), then frozen → zero-forgetting.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M': 'set of frozen experts', 'E_i': 'experience i', 'C_i': 'class subset seen by expert i'}
primitives.assumptions: Each expert is trained on disjoint class subsets and remains static post-training.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When repetition is absent, replay methods outperform frozen ensembles.

layer2.mapping: Each frozen expert mirrors a team's specialized role in a repetitive NFL season, where roles re-emerge across matchups.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy on repeated classes post-stream training.

primitives.name: Reliability Weighted Logits
primitives.verbatim_quote: Unified head over all classes learned via pseudo-feature projection (mean + std) aligning FEs that never saw a class, with cross-entropy + metric-learning loss balanced by adaptive alpha.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'k': 'class index', 'M': 'set of active experts', '\\text{logit}_{i,k}': 'logit from expert i for class k', '\\text{entropy}_{i,k}': "entropy of expert i's prediction for class k", 'N_C^{(i)}': 'number of classes seen by expert i', '\\text{feature\\_norm}_{i,k}': 'normalized feature norm for class k from expert i'}
primitives.assumptions: Experts are weighted by their confidence and class coverage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inference fails when expert entropy is high or class coverage is low.

layer2.mapping: Ensemble logits are derived from individual expert reliability scores, enabling robust classification under repetition.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-entropy loss on unseen classes after full stream training.

primitives.name: OOD Detection Branching
primitives.verbatim_quote: t treatment at inference: each branch first judged on whether the sample is OOD for it (mask or weight by OOD score), killing DER's overconfident-unseen-class problem.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'i': 'expert branch index', '\\text{logits}_i': 'logits from expert i', '\\text{feature\\_norm}_i': 'feature norm for expert i', '\\text{OOD\\_score}_i': 'out-of-distribution score for expert i'}
primitives.assumptions: Each expert branch independently assesses OOD status using softmax and feature norms.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Branches fail to detect OOD when feature norms are misaligned or logits are overconfident.

layer2.mapping: Each expert branch applies OOD scoring to prevent overconfidence on unseen classes, mimicking NFL’s unpredictability.
layer2.telemetry: False positive rate on unseen classes during inference.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight from the paper is that continual learning under repetition demands a shift from monolithic replay systems to frozen expert ensembles. In NFL contexts, this translates to treating each team's strategic repertoire as a distinct experience, where repetition occurs through recurring matchups, schemes, and personnel pairings. The frozen expert ensemble ensures zero-forgetting by locking in knowledge from previous experiences, while the unified head allows for coherent inference across all classes. The reliability-weighted logits provide a mechanism to aggregate expert outputs based on confidence and coverage, ensuring that specialists who have seen more classes contribute more to the final prediction. OOD detection prevents overconfident predictions on novel matchups, aligning with the NFL's unpredictable nature. These primitives form a dual framework: one for retention (frozen experts) and one for integration (reliability-weighted logits and OOD detection). The failure mode arises when repetition is mischaracterized or when experts are not properly isolated, leading to catastrophic forgetting or overfitting to outdated patterns.
